title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-p19p: C EDHOC TH_2 computation not CBOR-encoded (interop breakage)
description:
The commit cfc564a correctly fixed TH_2 computation in Rust (edhoc.rs transcript_2) and Python (edhoc.py) to use CBOR bstr encoding per RFC 9528 Section 3.2, but the C implementation at lichen/subsys/lichen/edhoc/edhoc.c was NOT updated.

**C code bug (both initiator and responder paths):**

Initiator path (line 749-764):
- Comment says 'TH_2 = H(H(message_1) || G_Y || C_R) per RFC 9528 Section 4.1.2'
- Actual code: th2_input = h_msg1 || g_y || c_r (raw concatenation)
- CORRECT: TH_2 = SHA-256(CBOR_bstr(G_Y) || CBOR_bstr(H(message_1)))

Responder path (line 1197-1212):
- Same bug: th2_input = h_msg1 || eph_pk || c_r (raw concatenation)
- Same fix needed

**Three issues:**
1. Missing CBOR bstr encoding on each component (should use zcbor_bstr_encode_ptr)
2. Wrong order: h_msg1 before g_y instead of g_y before h_msg1
3. Extraneous C_R included — RFC 9528 defines TH_2 = H(G_Y, H(message_1)), only two inputs

Ironically, the C code already has a correct compute_th() function with CBOR encoding (used for TH_3/TH_4) but doesn't use it for TH_2.

**Impact:** C-built LICHEN nodes cannot interoperate with Rust/Python nodes because they derive different TH_2 values, leading to different derived keys.
